# Tool reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen-docs.js from src/tools — do not edit by hand. -->

Every non-read-only tool also accepts `confirm` (a single-use approval token returned by a `CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED` error; only valid after the user approved that exact action).

Errors are returned as `{"error": {"code", "message", "hint", "recoverable", "details"}}` with codes: `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, `NOT_FOUND`, `TIMEOUT`, `PERMISSION_DENIED`, `POLICY_DENIED`, `CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED`, `KILL_SWITCH`, `UNSUPPORTED`, `DEPENDENCY_MISSING`, `BACKEND_FAILED`, `APP_NOT_RUNNING`, `VERIFICATION_FAILED`, `CANCELLED`, `INTERNAL`.

## env_inspect

**Inspect the computer.** Learn about the computer before acting: OS/hardware (system), display server (session), monitors (displays), shells, installed developer tools with versions (tools), what computer-control features work here and what to install if not (capabilities), important folders (dirs), installed GUI apps (apps), top processes (processes), and the safety level (safety). Results are cached on disk and reused across sessions; pass refresh=true after installing things.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sections` | `system`, `session`, `displays`, `shells`, `tools`, `capabilities`, `dirs`, `apps`, `processes`, `safety`, `all`[] |  | Default: system, session, displays, shells, tools, capabilities, dirs, safety. |
| `refresh` | boolean |  |  |

## workflow_search

**Search learned workflows.** ALWAYS call this before operating an application for a task. Searches the persistent workflow memory (learned + project + built-in) by task description and/or app. Returns status: "known" (reliable, verified workflow — run it), "partial" (a related/stale/failing workflow — run it carefully or use its steps as a guide), or "unknown" (explore the app; record what works). Each result has confidence, reasons, parameters, and last-verified date. Also reports what is known about the app itself.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `query` | string |  | The task, e.g. "export the project as png". |
| `app` | string |  | Restrict to an application. |
| `app_version` | string |  | Installed app version, to flag version mismatches. |
| `limit` | integer |  |  |

## workflow_get

**Get a workflow.** Return a workflow document by id (steps, parameters, expectations, failure modes, stats, version history).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes |  |
| `include_history` | boolean |  |  |

## workflow_run

**Run a workflow.** Execute a saved workflow step by step. Each step's tool call goes through the normal safety policy; each step's `expect` checks are verified (with retries/recovery as defined). Outcomes: succeeded (stats updated), failed (stops at the failing step with diagnosis, screenshot and a recovery guide — adapt, finish the task, then workflow_save an improved version), paused (a manual step needs you; resume with start_at), blocked (needs user approval), precondition_failed. dry_run shows the resolved steps without doing anything.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes |  |
| `params` | object |  | Values for the workflow's {{parameters}}. |
| `start_at` | string |  | Resume from this step id. |
| `stop_after` | string |  | Stop after this step id. |
| `dry_run` | boolean |  |  |
| `record_outcome` | boolean |  | Update reliability stats (default true). |

## workflow_save

**Save a workflow.** Persist a workflow you discovered or improved, so future sessions reuse it instead of exploring again. Saving an existing id creates a new version (old one archived). Set verified=true only if you just completed the task successfully with these steps. Shape: {"name","app":{"name","version?","tested_version?"},"description","triggers":[...],"parameters":[{"name","description","required","default"}],"preconditions":[checks],"steps":[{"id","title","action":{"tool","args"} | "manual":"instruction","expect":[checks],"timeout_ms","retries","on_failure","hints":{"location","shortcut","notes"}}],"expected_results":[checks],"failure_modes":[{"symptom","recovery"}],"notes":[...]}. Use {{param}} placeholders in args/checks. Prefer text targets over raw coordinates. scope "project" stores it in the repo (.computer-skills/workflows) to share with the team.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workflow` | object | yes | The workflow document. |
| `scope` | `user`, `project` |  |  |
| `change_note` | string |  | What changed and why (for updates). |
| `verified` | boolean |  | The task was just completed successfully with exactly these steps. |
| `reset_stats` | boolean |  | Reset reliability stats (use when the procedure changed fundamentally). |
| `merge` | boolean |  | Merge into the existing workflow instead of replacing it. |

## workflow_feedback

**Report a workflow outcome.** Record whether a workflow worked when you executed it manually or resumed it mid-way (workflow_run records full runs automatically). Updates its reliability and last-verified date.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes |  |
| `success` | boolean | yes |  |
| `reason` | string |  | Failure reason or note. |
| `step` | string |  | Failing step id. |
| `app_version` | string |  |  |

## workflow_record

**Record a workflow while learning.** Capture your actions while you work out how to do something in an app. "start" (name, app), then act normally — successful action-tool calls are recorded as steps and successful verify calls become the previous step's expectations; "annotate" adds a note to the last step; "status"; "stop" returns a draft workflow (not saved) with cleanup advice; "discard".

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action` | `start`, `stop`, `status`, `annotate`, `discard` | yes |  |
| `name` | string |  |  |
| `app` | string |  |  |
| `description` | string |  |  |
| `note` | string |  |  |

## app_profile

**App knowledge.** Knowledge about an application independent of any single task: built-in adapter knowledge (shortcuts, menus, scripting, pitfalls) plus what you learned before. "get" before exploring an app; "update" after learning something reusable (patch: {"shortcuts": {...}, "ui_map": {"<control>": {"location", "how"}}, "menus": {...}, "quirks": [...], "notes": [...], "version": "x.y"}); "list".

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action` | `get`, `update`, `list` | yes |  |
| `app` | string |  |  |
| `patch` | object |  |  |

## terminal_run

**Run a command.** Run one shell command to completion and return exit code, stdout and stderr (ANSI stripped, long output truncated in the middle). Picks the right shell for the OS ("auto": your $SHELL/bash on Linux/macOS, pwsh/powershell on Windows) or use `shell`. Failures include a `failure` object {category: not-found|permission|network|locked|syntax|timeout|..., retryable, hint}. Use `retries` for flaky network operations. For long-running servers/watchers use `process` (action start); for stateful/interactive work use `terminal_session`. Commands are risk-classified: destructive or system-changing commands may require the user's approval.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `command` | string | yes | The command line to execute. |
| `shell` | `auto`, `bash`, `zsh`, `fish`, `sh`, `dash`, `ksh`, `pwsh`, `powershell`, `cmd` |  | Shell to use (default auto). |
| `cwd` | string |  | Working directory (default: the project directory). |
| `env` | object |  | Extra environment variables. |
| `timeout_ms` | integer |  | Kill the command after this long (default 120000). |
| `stdin` | string |  | Text piped to the command's standard input. |
| `login` | boolean |  | Run as a login shell (loads profile files; slower). |
| `retries` | integer |  | Retry failed runs (with backoff) when the failure is retryable. |
| `retry_on` | `retryable`, `network`, `any` |  | Which failures to retry (default retryable). |

## terminal_session

**Interactive terminal session.** Persistent terminal sessions whose state (cwd, env, activated venvs, REPL variables) survives between calls. Actions: "start" (a shell, or `program` such as "python3 -i", "node", "ssh host"; `pty`=true gives a real pseudo-terminal on Linux/macOS for programs that need one), "send" (write `input`; for shells it waits until the command finishes and returns its exit_code; for programs it waits for `wait_for` regex or until output is idle), "read" (new output since last read; optionally wait for a regex), "signal" (SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGKILL, e.g. to stop a running command), "close", "list".

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action` | `start`, `send`, `read`, `signal`, `close`, `list` | yes |  |
| `session` | string |  | Session id or name (send/read/signal/close). |
| `name` | string |  | Friendly name for a new session. |
| `shell` | `auto`, `bash`, `zsh`, `fish`, `sh`, `dash`, `ksh`, `pwsh`, `powershell`, `cmd` |  |  |
| `program` | string |  | Run this program instead of a shell (e.g. "python3 -i"). |
| `pty` | boolean |  | Allocate a pseudo-terminal (Linux/macOS). |
| `cwd` | string |  |  |
| `env` | object |  |  |
| `input` | string |  | Text to send (a command for shells). |
| `newline` | boolean |  | Append a newline to input (default true). |
| `complete` | boolean |  | Wait for the shell command to complete and report its exit code (default true for shells). |
| `wait_for` | string |  | Regex to wait for in the output (e.g. a prompt like ">>> $"). |
| `timeout_ms` | integer |  | Max time to wait (default 30000). |
| `idle_ms` | integer |  | For programs: return once output is idle this long (default 800). |
| `signal` | `SIGINT`, `SIGTERM`, `SIGKILL`, `SIGHUP` |  |  |
| `all` | boolean |  | read: return the whole buffer, not just new output. |
| `force` | boolean |  | close: kill immediately. |

## process

**Background & system processes.** Manage long-running background processes (dev servers, watchers, builds) and inspect OS processes. Actions: "start" (run `command` in the background with logs captured; wait for readiness via `ready_pattern` regex in output or `ready_port`), "status", "logs" (tail/grep the captured log), "stop" (managed process), "list" (managed processes), "system" (OS process table, `filter` by name/pid), "kill" (an OS process by `pid`; risky).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action` | `start`, `status`, `logs`, `stop`, `list`, `system`, `kill` | yes |  |
| `id` | string |  | Managed process id or name. |
| `command` | string |  |  |
| `name` | string |  |  |
| `shell` | `auto`, `bash`, `zsh`, `fish`, `sh`, `dash`, `ksh`, `pwsh`, `powershell`, `cmd` |  |  |
| `cwd` | string |  |  |
| `env` | object |  |  |
| `ready_pattern` | string |  | Regex that signals readiness, e.g. "listening on\|ready in". |
| `ready_port` | integer |  | TCP port that signals readiness when it accepts connections. |
| `ready_timeout_ms` | integer |  |  |
| `tail` | integer |  | logs: number of lines (default 100). |
| `grep` | string |  | logs: only lines matching this regex. |
| `force` | boolean |  |  |
| `pid` | integer |  | kill: OS process id. |
| `filter` | string |  | system: name or pid filter. |
| `limit` | integer |  |  |

## app

**Applications.** Discover, launch, inspect and quit desktop applications. Actions: "find" (search installed apps by name — use before launching an unfamiliar app), "launch" (start by `name` or `path`, waits until its window appears and returns it; if already running it focuses it unless if_running="new"), "status" (running? windows? focused?), "quit" (graceful; reports if a "save changes?" dialog blocks it; force=true kills), "open" (open a file/folder/URL with its default app; reveal=true shows it in the file manager), "adapters" (apps with built-in knowledge/scripting).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action` | `find`, `launch`, `status`, `quit`, `open`, `adapters` | yes |  |
| `name` | string |  | Application name, e.g. "Blender", "firefox", "Visual Studio Code". |
| `path` | string |  | Executable/app bundle path (launch), or file/URL (open). |
| `args` | string[] |  | Command-line arguments (launch). |
| `params` | object |  | Adapter launch parameters, e.g. {"file": "scene.blend"}, {"url": "..."}, {"project": "..."}. |
| `cwd` | string |  |  |
| `wait` | boolean |  | Wait for the window (default true). |
| `timeout_ms` | integer |  | How long to wait for the window (default 30000). |
| `if_running` | `focus`, `new` |  | Behaviour when the app is already running (default focus). |
| `pid` | integer |  |  |
| `force` | boolean |  | quit: kill without saving. |
| `reveal` | boolean |  | open: reveal in file manager instead of opening. |
| `limit` | integer |  |  |
| `refresh` | boolean |  | find: rescan installed applications. |

## app_script

**Run an app's scripting interface.** Automate an application through its native scripting/CLI interface instead of the GUI — far more reliable when available. Blender: Python/bpy (`code`; background=true runs headless and returns stdout; `file` opens a .blend first). Godot: GDScript (`code` extending SceneTree, optional options.project) or raw `args`. Unity: options {project, method} (-executeMethod, batch mode). Chrome/Chromium/Edge: options {operation: dump_dom|screenshot|pdf, url, output}. VS Code: `args` for the code CLI. Photoshop: ExtendScript `code`. Use app action "adapters" to list what is installed. Code is risk-classified (file deletion / subprocesses need approval).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `app` | string | yes | Adapter id or app name (blender, godot, unity, chrome, chromium, edge, firefox, vscode, photoshop). |
| `code` | string |  | Script source in the app's language. |
| `file` | string |  | Document/project to open first (e.g. a .blend file). |
| `args` | string[] |  | Raw CLI arguments (adapters that accept them). |
| `background` | boolean |  | Run headless where supported (default true). |
| `options` | object |  | Adapter-specific options (e.g. {"operation": "pdf", "url": "...", "output": "..."}). |
| `executable` | string |  | Override the app executable path. |
| `timeout_ms` | integer |  |  |

## window

**Windows.** List and manage windows. Actions: "list" (all top-level windows with id, title, app, pid, bounds, focused), "active" (the focused window), "focus", "minimize", "maximize", "restore", "fullscreen", "close" (asks the app to close; it may prompt to save), "move" (x,y), "resize" (width,height). Select the window with window_id (exact), title (fuzzy), title_regex, app or pid. Focus a window before sending keyboard input to it.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action` | `list`, `active`, `focus`, `minimize`, `maximize`, `restore`, `fullscreen`, `close`, `move`, `resize` | yes |  |
| `window_id` | string |  | Exact window id from window list. |
| `title` | string |  | Window title (fuzzy match). |
| `title_regex` | string |  | Regex matched against the window title. |
| `app` | string |  | Application/process name that owns the window. |
| `pid` | integer |  | Owning process id. |
| `x` | integer |  |  |
| `y` | integer |  |  |
| `width` | integer |  |  |
| `height` | integer |  |  |
| `filter` | string |  | list: only windows whose title/app contains this text. |

## screen_capture

**Screenshot.** Capture the screen, a window (by selector) or a region and return the image plus a screenshot_id. Images are downscaled to max_width (default 1568px) — the result explains how image pixels map to screen coordinates, or pass screenshot_id with image coordinates to input_mouse and it converts for you. Use this to observe state before and after actions.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `window_id` | string |  | Exact window id from window list. |
| `title` | string |  | Window title (fuzzy match). |
| `title_regex` | string |  | Regex matched against the window title. |
| `app` | string |  | Application/process name that owns the window. |
| `pid` | integer |  | Owning process id. |
| `region` | object |  | Screen rectangle in logical screen coordinates. |
| `max_width` | integer |  |  |
| `include_image` | boolean |  | Return the image (default true). false = only save to disk and return metadata. |
| `screens` | boolean |  | Also return monitor layout. |

## screen_text

**Read text on screen (OCR).** Extract visible text from the screen, a window or a region with OCR (Vision on macOS, Windows.Media.Ocr on Windows, tesseract anywhere). Returns lines with screen-coordinate bounding boxes (and words), so you can locate labels to click. Works for apps without accessibility support.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `window_id` | string |  | Exact window id from window list. |
| `title` | string |  | Window title (fuzzy match). |
| `title_regex` | string |  | Regex matched against the window title. |
| `app` | string |  | Application/process name that owns the window. |
| `pid` | integer |  | Owning process id. |
| `region` | object |  | Screen rectangle in logical screen coordinates. |
| `min_confidence` | integer |  | Drop lines below this OCR confidence (default 30). |
| `words` | boolean |  | Include per-word boxes (default false). |
| `contains` | string |  | Only return lines containing this text (case-insensitive). |

## ui_inspect

**Inspect UI (accessibility tree).** Read a window's accessibility tree (UI Automation on Windows, AX on macOS, AT-SPI on Linux): roles, names, values, bounds, available actions, each with an element id ("el-…") usable by ui_action / input_mouse. format="flat" with interactive_only=true gives a compact list of controls. Apps that draw their own UI (Blender, games, some Electron/Java apps) expose little or nothing — then use screen_capture + screen_text.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `window_id` | string |  | Exact window id from window list. |
| `title` | string |  | Window title (fuzzy match). |
| `title_regex` | string |  | Regex matched against the window title. |
| `app` | string |  | Application/process name that owns the window. |
| `pid` | integer |  | Owning process id. |
| `depth` | integer |  | Max tree depth (default 8). |
| `max_nodes` | integer |  | Node budget (default 300). |
| `format` | `tree`, `flat` |  |  |
| `interactive_only` | boolean |  | flat: only buttons, fields, menu items, etc. |
| `include_menus` | boolean |  | macOS: include the menu bar. |

## ui_find

**Find UI elements.** Locate controls or text by visible label (and/or role) in a window or on screen. method "auto" tries the accessibility tree first and falls back to OCR; force one with "a11y" or "ocr". Returns ranked matches with element id, bounds, center point and score. Use the element id with ui_action or input_mouse.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `text` | string |  | Visible label/text to look for (fuzzy). |
| `role` | string |  | Role filter, e.g. button, menu item, edit, checkbox, tab. |
| `window_id` | string |  | Exact window id from window list. |
| `title` | string |  | Window title (fuzzy match). |
| `title_regex` | string |  | Regex matched against the window title. |
| `app` | string |  | Application/process name that owns the window. |
| `pid` | integer |  | Owning process id. |
| `region` | object |  | Screen rectangle in logical screen coordinates. |
| `method` | `auto`, `a11y`, `ocr` |  |  |
| `exact` | boolean |  | Require an exact (case-insensitive) text match. |
| `limit` | integer |  |  |

## ui_action

**Act on a UI element.** Perform a semantic action on an element: press/click, double_click, focus, set_value (text fields, sliders), toggle, expand, collapse, select. Target it by `element` id (from ui_find/ui_inspect) or by `text` (+ optional role and window selector; the best match is used). Uses accessibility actions when possible (works even if the control is covered) and falls back to clicking its center.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action` | `press`, `click`, `double_click`, `focus`, `set_value`, `toggle`, `expand`, `collapse`, `select` | yes |  |
| `element` | string |  | Element id from ui_find / ui_inspect. |
| `text` | string |  | Find the element by label instead of id. |
| `role` | string |  |  |
| `window_id` | string |  | Exact window id from window list. |
| `title` | string |  | Window title (fuzzy match). |
| `title_regex` | string |  | Regex matched against the window title. |
| `app` | string |  | Application/process name that owns the window. |
| `pid` | integer |  | Owning process id. |
| `value` | string \| number \| boolean |  | set_value: the new value. |

## ui_menu

**Select a menu item.** Open a menu path in an application, e.g. ["File", "Export", "PNG"]. Uses the native menu API (macOS menu bar, Windows UI Automation) when available, otherwise navigates visually (finds each label with accessibility/OCR and clicks it). Labels match fuzzily and ignore "..." suffixes.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string[] | yes | Menu labels from the menu bar to the item. |
| `window_id` | string |  | Exact window id from window list. |
| `title` | string |  | Window title (fuzzy match). |
| `title_regex` | string |  | Regex matched against the window title. |
| `app` | string |  | Application/process name that owns the window. |
| `pid` | integer |  | Owning process id. |
| `method` | `auto`, `native`, `visual` |  |  |
| `delay_ms` | integer |  | visual: wait after each click (default 350). |

## ui_dialog

**Handle dialogs.** Deal with dialogs, message boxes and file pickers. Actions: "detect" (list open dialogs), "read" (dialog text via OCR + its buttons), "accept" (press the affirmative button: Save/OK/Open/Yes… or Enter), "cancel" (Cancel/No/Close or Escape), "press" (a specific `button` label), "fill_path" (type `path` into a native Open/Save dialog using the OS's reliable keyboard method, then submit). Without a selector, the most likely dialog (focused/newest) is used. Read a dialog before accepting it.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action` | `detect`, `read`, `accept`, `cancel`, `press`, `fill_path` | yes |  |
| `window_id` | string |  | Exact window id from window list. |
| `title` | string |  | Window title (fuzzy match). |
| `title_regex` | string |  | Regex matched against the window title. |
| `app` | string |  | Application/process name that owns the window. |
| `pid` | integer |  | Owning process id. |
| `button` | string |  | press: button label. |
| `path` | string |  | fill_path: file path to enter. |
| `mode` | `open`, `save` |  | fill_path: dialog kind (auto-detected from the title). |
| `submit` | boolean |  | fill_path: press Enter afterwards (default true). |

## input_mouse

**Mouse.** Move, click, drag and scroll. Target with `element` (id from ui_find/ui_inspect), `text` (label found via accessibility/OCR — robust to layout changes), or x/y screen coordinates (add `screenshot_id` to give coordinates in that screenshot's image space). Actions: move, click, double_click, right_click, middle_click, down, up, drag (to to_x/to_y, to_element or to_text), scroll (dy>0 scrolls down, dx>0 right; or direction+amount), position. `modifiers` (e.g. ["shift"]) are held during the click. Verify the effect afterwards (screenshot/verify).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action` | `move`, `click`, `double_click`, `right_click`, `middle_click`, `down`, `up`, `drag`, `scroll`, `position` | yes |  |
| `x` | number |  |  |
| `y` | number |  |  |
| `screenshot_id` | string |  | Interpret x/y (and to_x/to_y) in this screenshot's image coordinates. |
| `element` | string |  |  |
| `text` | string |  |  |
| `role` | string |  |  |
| `window_id` | string |  | Exact window id from window list. |
| `title` | string |  | Window title (fuzzy match). |
| `title_regex` | string |  | Regex matched against the window title. |
| `app` | string |  | Application/process name that owns the window. |
| `pid` | integer |  | Owning process id. |
| `to_x` | number |  |  |
| `to_y` | number |  |  |
| `to_element` | string |  |  |
| `to_text` | string |  |  |
| `button` | `left`, `right`, `middle` |  |  |
| `modifiers` | string[] |  | Keys held during the click, e.g. ["ctrl"] or ["shift"]. |
| `dx` | integer |  |  |
| `dy` | integer |  |  |
| `direction` | `up`, `down`, `left`, `right` |  |  |
| `amount` | integer |  | scroll: number of wheel steps (default 3). |
| `duration_ms` | integer |  | drag: duration. |
| `focus_window` | boolean |  | Focus the selected window first (default true when a window selector is given). |

## input_keyboard

**Keyboard.** Type text or press keys in the focused window (or focus a window first via the selector). Actions: "type" (text; method "paste" uses the clipboard — fast and exact for long/unicode text), "press" (a key or combo: "enter", "ctrl+s", "mod+shift+p", ["alt","f4"]; `mod` = Cmd on macOS, Ctrl elsewhere; `repeat` presses N times), "hold"/"release" (keep a key down). Prefer app shortcuts and terminal_run over typing commands into terminals. Typing into a terminal window is risk-classified as a command.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action` | `type`, `press`, `hold`, `release` | yes |  |
| `text` | string |  | type: the text ("\n" presses Enter). |
| `keys` | string \| string[] |  | press/hold/release: e.g. "mod+s" or ["ctrl","shift","t"]. |
| `repeat` | integer |  |  |
| `method` | `auto`, `keys`, `paste` |  |  |
| `delay_ms` | integer |  | type: delay between keystrokes. |
| `window_id` | string |  | Exact window id from window list. |
| `title` | string |  | Window title (fuzzy match). |
| `title_regex` | string |  | Regex matched against the window title. |
| `app` | string |  | Application/process name that owns the window. |
| `pid` | integer |  | Owning process id. |

## clipboard

**Clipboard.** Read or write the system clipboard text. Useful for moving text in/out of apps exactly (copy with mod+c then read).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action` | `read`, `write` | yes |  |
| `text` | string |  |  |

## verify

**Verify / wait for conditions.** Check observable evidence instead of assuming an action worked — and wait for it. Evaluates `checks` (window_exists, window_absent, window_focused, text_visible, text_absent, element_exists, file_exists, file_absent, file_contains, process_running, process_absent, port_open, http_ok, command_succeeds, screen_changed, clipboard_contains), polling until they pass or `timeout_ms` elapses (0 = check once). Returns per-check evidence. Example: after launching, {"checks":[{"type":"window_exists","app":"blender"}],"timeout_ms":20000}; after saving, {"checks":[{"type":"file_exists","path":"out.png","modified_within_s":60}]}.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `checks` | object[] | yes | Conditions to verify. |
| `timeout_ms` | integer |  | Keep polling up to this long (default 0). |
| `interval_ms` | integer |  |  |
| `mode` | `all`, `any` |  | Pass when all (default) or any checks pass. |
| `screenshot_on_failure` | boolean |  | Attach a screenshot if verification fails (default false). |

## diagnose

**Diagnose the current state.** When something did not go as expected: summarises what is going on — focused window, whether the app is still running (crash), open dialogs and their text/buttons, focus problems, recent app log output — with concrete recovery suggestions. Optionally attaches a screenshot.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `app` | string |  | The application you were working with. |
| `include_screenshot` | boolean |  | Attach a screenshot (default true). |
| `read_dialogs` | boolean |  | OCR open dialogs (default true). |

## safety

**Safety policy.** Inspect the safety policy: "status" (level, what each risk level requires, kill switch, config sources), "check" (dry-run risk classification of a `command` — nothing is executed), "audit" (recent policy decisions), "stop" (engage the kill switch: all actions are refused until the user resumes). The level itself can only be changed by the user.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action` | `status`, `check`, `audit`, `stop` | yes |  |
| `command` | string |  |  |
| `limit` | integer |  |  |
| `reason` | string |  |  |

## Verification checks

Used by `verify`, workflow step `expect`, `preconditions` and `expected_results`.

| Type | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `window_exists` | A window matching {title|title_regex|app|pid|window_id} exists |
| `window_absent` | No window matches the selector |
| `window_focused` | The focused window matches the selector |
| `text_visible` | OCR/accessibility finds {text} (or {regex}) on screen, optionally within {window selector} or {region} |
| `text_absent` | The text is not visible |
| `element_exists` | An accessibility element named {text} (optional {role}) exists in the window |
| `file_exists` | File {path} exists (optional {min_bytes}, {modified_within_s}, {modified_after_start}) |
| `file_absent` | File {path} does not exist |
| `file_contains` | File {path} contains {text} or matches {regex} |
| `process_running` | A process named {name} or with {pid} is running |
| `process_absent` | No such process is running |
| `port_open` | TCP {port} on {host=127.0.0.1} accepts connections |
| `http_ok` | GET {url} returns {status=2xx} (optional {contains}) |
| `command_succeeds` | Shell {command} exits 0 (optional {stdout_regex}) |
| `screen_changed` | The screen (or {region}) changed by at least {min_fraction=0.01} since {screenshot_id} |
| `clipboard_contains` | Clipboard contains {text} |

Window-related checks accept `window_id`, `title` (fuzzy), `title_regex`, `app`, `pid`. Any check accepts a `label` echoed back in results.
